//: The places of src/ that read a `trap` command by its name, or a signal word as EXIT, outside the walk (test/trap-source.test.ts). None decides the trap in effect at a statement; each has its reason. The list may only shrink.

uses.reason: the dialect check of `trap … ERR` (`trapErr`): whether the shell knows the ERR signal, a feature of the shell, not the trap in effect
`where === 'trap'` compares a value of `inFunction` (src/semantics/env.ts), where `local` runs, not a command name
the idiom `trap … EXIT` (`idiom-exit-trap`) is found by the words as written, also on a line the walk did not run; its signal words through `trappedName`
the idiom reads the signal words through the walk's own reader, `trappedName`, so that it takes for EXIT what bash takes (`exit`, `00`)
the usage error of a lone `trap INT` in POSIX mode (a special builtin's error ends the shell), not the trap in effect
the trust scan reads the action of every `trap` before the walk runs, to find strings it cannot read (a DEBUG or RETURN trap makes nothing trusted)
